# experiments/inksight/CRITERIA.md
# PRE-REGISTRATION — InkSight vs Skeleton Trajectory-Recovery Evaluation
#
# STATUS  : LOCKED — written before any inference run.
# RULE    : Do NOT edit this file after the first commit that contains it.
#           All thresholds and statistical procedures are fixed here.

**Commit date (pre-run lock):** 2026-10-07
**Experiment directory:** `experiments/inksight/`
**Model:** InkSight Small-p (`Derendering/InkSight-Small-p` on HuggingFace)

---

## 1. Purpose

Decide whether InkSight is **"useful"** for our kinematics pipeline — i.e.,
whether it recovers Latin-script handwriting trajectories well enough to
replace skeleton-based recovery.  
A **"useful" verdict requires ALL three primary gates (§9 P1–P3) to pass.**  
Failure on any gate means "not useful". Report results as-is; no tuning
permitted on the test set.

---

## 2. Three Methods Under Comparison

| Label | Description |
|---|---|
| **GT** | Ground-truth tablet strokes — pen-on-paper only (see §4) |
| **InkSight** | InkSight Small-p on the 224×224 padded word image |
| **Skeleton** | Our existing skeleton-based recovery, run on the **same 224×224 padded image** as InkSight (see §5) |

---

## 3. Fairness Constraint (§5)

> Both InkSight **and** Skeleton receive the identical 224×224 white-padded
> JPEG crop. Skeleton must **not** receive the raw full-resolution tablet image.
> This input-parity rule is fixed before running.

Rationale: padding and resizing alter spatial relationships. Skeleton run on
full-res would have an unfair information advantage.

---

## 4. Ground Truth Definition

GT = **pen-on-paper strokes only**:
- Include strokes where `pen_status == down` (or pressure > 0).
- **Exclude** air strokes (pen lifted, moving between contact segments).
- Applies to dataSciRep and DiaGraMo TSK4/TSK16.
- GT is rendered from tablet data using our existing renderer, cropped to GT
  word bounding boxes so segmentation is not a confound.

---

## 5. Round-Trip Coordinate Mapping Test — MUST PASS BEFORE ANY REAL RUN

Before processing any real sample, execute the following test and assert it
passes:

1. Render a known GT word trajectory to a 224×224 padded image using the
   same pad/resize pipeline used for inference.
2. Transform the known GT (x, y) coordinates through the pad/resize map
   into 224×224 space.
3. Apply the inverse transform back to original tablet pixel space.
4. Assert: **max absolute coordinate error < 0.5 px** (half-pixel, in
   original tablet pixel units) across all GT points.

If this test fails, stop. Fix the coordinate transform. Do not run inference
until the round-trip error is < 0.5 px. Log the actual max error in results.

---

## 6. Normalisation (applied before all metric computation)

Identical pipeline for GT, InkSight, and Skeleton:

1. **Inverse pad/resize:** Map 224×224 pixel coordinates back to real tablet
   pixel space (after round-trip test §5 passes).
2. **H_med normalisation:** Divide all coordinates by H_med — the median word
   height computed from GT, **per subject**, in real tablet pixel units.
3. **Arc-length resampling (DTW only):** Resample each trajectory to N=100
   equally-spaced arc-length points before DTW.
   Chamfer uses raw normalised point sets without resampling.

---

## 7. Sampling

- **Datasets:** dataSciRep + DiaGraMo TSK4/TSK16 word-level GT trajectories.
- **Sample by subject** (not by word). Fixed seed: `SEED = 42`.
- **N = 50 subjects**, balanced by label (dysgraphic / control).  
  If a label has fewer than 25 subjects, use all available; report actual N.
- **Test set:** Hold out **20 subjects (10 per label)** before looking at any
  results. All sanity checks and per-variant diagnostics are done on the
  remaining 30. All primary metric tables and pass/fail verdicts use the
  **test set only**.
- **Per-subject grouping:** All word samples from a subject stay together.
  Subject is the unit of analysis for all statistical tests.
- **Image variants per word:** clean, ruled-paper, grid-paper, Gaussian-blur,
  camera-like noise. All five variants run per word. Metrics broken down by
  variant in secondary reporting.

---

## 8. Metrics — Fixed Definitions

### 8a. Spatial

| Metric | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Chamfer distance** | Mean of (nearest-GT-point distance for each predicted point) + (nearest-predicted-point distance for each GT point); H_med units; per word, averaged to subject level |
| **DTW distance** | Dynamic Time Warping on arc-length-resampled (N=100) trajectories; H_med units; per word, averaged to subject level |

### 8b. Structural

| Metric | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Stroke count error** | `|predicted_stroke_count − GT_stroke_count|`; per word |
| **Per-stroke direction correctness** | Fraction of strokes where predicted start→end direction agrees with GT within ±90°; per word |
| **Stroke order accuracy** | Fraction of GT stroke-pairs (i, j) with i < j for which predicted strokes are also ordered i before j; per word |
| **Pen-up/down F1** | Token-level F1 at N=100 arc-length-resampled positions (pen-down=1, pen-up=0); reported if stroke alignment is feasible; otherwise "N/A" |

### 8c. Geometric Features — Spearman Correlation to GT

Computed from **(x, y) only — no timing required**.  
Subject-level: compute mean feature value per subject across all their words;
then Spearman ρ across subjects between predicted and GT values.

| Feature | Formula |
|---|---|
| Mean absolute curvature | Mean of |κ| along arc; κ estimated from consecutive point triplets |
| Turn density | Direction reversals per unit arc length |
| Tortuosity | Arc length / straight-line start-to-end distance |
| Path length ratio | Total arc length / GT bounding-box diagonal |

### 8d. Effect-Size Analysis (Dysgraphic vs Control)

For each feature F and each method M ∈ {GT, InkSight, Skeleton}:

- Compute subject-level mean of F.
- Compute **subject-level Cohen's d** (dysgraphic mean − control mean) / pooled SD.
- Compute **bootstrap 95% CI** on Cohen's d: B=2000 resamples of subjects
  with replacement, BCa method.
- **Effect-size retention:**  
  `retention(M, F) = Cohen's_d(M, F) / Cohen's_d(GT, F)`  
  If GT d = 0 for feature F, report that feature's retention as "N/A".

---

## 9. Statistical Testing — "Beats" Definition

> "InkSight **beats** Skeleton on metric X" means:
>
> The **paired bootstrap 95% CI** of  
> `mean_subjects( X_skeleton − X_inksight )`  
> **excludes 0**, with sign consistent with InkSight being better.
>
> Parameters: B=2000 resamples of subjects with replacement, BCa method.
> Computed on **test-set subjects only**.

Lower is better for Chamfer and DTW.  
Higher is better for Spearman ρ, direction correctness, stroke order accuracy,
pen-up/down F1, and effect-size retention.

---

## 10. Pass/Fail Gates

### PRIMARY GATES — All three must pass for a "useful" verdict

| Gate | Criterion |
|---|---|
| **P1 — Chamfer** | InkSight beats Skeleton on Chamfer distance (paired bootstrap 95% CI excludes 0, lower is better) |
| **P2 — Feature Spearman** | InkSight beats Skeleton on ≥ 2 of 4 geometric-feature Spearman ρ values (bootstrap CI excludes 0 for each claimed win) |
| **P3 — Effect-size retention** | InkSight retains ≥ 80% of GT Cohen's d on ≥ 2 of 4 geometric features (bootstrap CI lower bound > 0.80 × GT d) |

### TOLERANCE GATE — "Not Meaningfully Worse" (Chamfer only)

Even if P1 fails, InkSight is deemed **"not meaningfully worse"** if:

> `mean_subject_Chamfer(InkSight) ≤ mean_subject_Chamfer(Skeleton) + 0.10`

where 0.10 is in H_med-normalised units.  
**This value (0.10) is fixed pre-run.**  
A "not meaningfully worse" result is reported as a nuance flag; it does NOT
upgrade a failed P1 to a pass.

### SECONDARY / DIAGNOSTIC GATES (reported; do not determine "useful")

| Gate | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **S1 — DTW** | InkSight vs Skeleton on DTW (informational) |
| **S2 — Structural** | Stroke count error, direction correctness, order accuracy per method |
| **S3 — Pen F1** | Pen-up/down F1 per method (if computable) |
| **S4 — Variant breakdown** | All metrics broken down by image variant |
| **S5 — Label breakdown** | All metrics broken down by dysgraphic / control |

---

## 11. Scope Limitation — Script Generalisation

> A positive (or negative) result on **Latin-script** data (Malay, dataSciRep,
> DiaGraMo) does **not** justify, and cannot be used to argue for, deployment
> on **Devanagari** or **Telugu** script.
>
> InkSight Small-p is trained on English, Chinese, Japanese, and Vietnamese.
> Devanagari and Telugu are out-of-distribution. A Latin win ≠ Devanagari
> capability. Any such claim is explicitly out of scope for this experiment.

Qualitative runs on Hindi school photos and Malay photos are for visual
inspection only. Document Devanagari failures (garbled output, wrong script,
wrong stroke count) but do not use these to compute pass/fail on §10.

---

## 12. Forbidden Metrics from InkSight Output

The following must **not** be computed or reported from InkSight (x, y)-only
output under any circumstances:

- Velocity, speed, acceleration, jerk
- NVI (Normalized Velocity Index)
- Sigma-Lognormal model parameters (D, t₀, μ, σ)
- Any feature requiring timestamps

InkSight produces no timing information. Fabricating timestamps from point
count or arc length is not permitted.

---

## 13. Failure Reporting Rules

- Report ALL samples including failures. Do not drop failed InkSight samples.
- If InkSight produces **empty output (0 strokes)** on a sample, record:
  - Chamfer = `inf`, DTW = `inf`
  - Stroke count error = GT stroke count
  - Direction correctness = 0, order accuracy = 0
- If the environment, weights, or CPU speed make the full 50-subject run
  infeasible, run a minimum of **20 subjects (10 per label)** and state this
  explicitly in the results summary.
- Do not round any number. Do not soften any finding.

---

## 15. What This Experiment Does NOT Do

- Does not modify `src/` or the main kinematics pipeline.
- Does not train or fine-tune any model.
- Does not perform classification or risk-scoring.
- Does not report velocity, jerk, NVI, or any timing-based feature from
  InkSight output.
- Does not use Devanagari qualitative observations to claim production readiness.
